guards.what: the ExtraDamage counter is per-COMBAT, not per-run -- the growth must not survive the combat that built it
guards.maps_to: `_extraDamage` is a private field of the enchantment instance and nothing in the source ever resets it (`grep -rn 'ExtraDamage' src/Core --include=*.cs` finds only the DynamicVar type of the same name). It is per-combat all the same, structurally: `PopulateCombatState` clones every deck card into the draw pile (Player.cs:802-811), the clone's enchantment comes from `ClonePreservingMutability` (CardModel.cs:1204-1209), and the DECK copy never plays -- so each combat starts from the deck version's untouched counter. The sim reaches the same place by the same shape: `RunState.create_combat` deep-copies the deck (sts2_rl/run.py). Pinned by test_momentum_starts_each_combat_at_zero, which plays the enchanted Strike twice in each of two combats and asserts 6, 11, 6, 11.

guards.what: a mid-combat card COPY carries the accumulated counter, not just the Amount
guards.maps_to: `ClonePreservingMutability` is `AbstractModel.MutableClone`, a MemberwiseClone, so every field of the enchantment rides along -- including `_extraDamage`. The sim's base `Enchantment.clone_preserving_mutability` copies only `amount` and `disabled`, so Momentum overrides it to carry `extra_damage`. Reachable with ported content: Momentum enchants Attacks and Anger is an Attack that copies itself on play (cards/anger.py), as does the Trash Heap's copy. Pinned by test_a_card_copy_carries_momentums_accumulated_bonus.
guards.issue: NOTED for the tier, not a gap here: the base helper copying two named fields where C# does a memberwise clone is a shape that will bite the next enchantment with private state. Momentum is the first one to have any -- the other 19 keep everything in `amount`/`disabled` -- so there is nothing else to fix today.

guards.what: the sole granter: Punch Dagger's pickup screen
guards.maps_to: `PunchDagger.AfterObtained` (PunchDagger.cs:24-33) builds a `CardSelectorPrefs(EnchantSelectionPrompt, 1)` -- the one-count ctor sets MinSelect == MaxSelect == 1 (CardSelectorPrefs.cs:62-66), so the pick is mandatory, not skippable -- runs `CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForEnchantment(owner, canonicalMomentum, 5, prefs)` and enchants the result with `DynamicVar("Momentum", 5m)` (:15-19). `sts2_rl/relics/punch_dagger.py`'s `after_obtained` is that: filter the deck by `MomentumEnchantment.can_enchant`, `run.select_cards('enchant', candidates, 1)`, attach at amount 5. There is NO shuffle here, unlike Royal Stamp's Niche shuffle, so the screen is built in deck order and the pickup costs no RNG draw. `CardCmd.Preview` on the tail is presentation. Pinned by test_punch_dagger_enchants_a_deck_attack_with_momentum_5 and by test_reward_dispatch_and_relic_stubs.py::test_punch_dagger_enchants_a_deck_attack_now_that_momentum_is_ported.
